long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani entered Qatar’s government in 1982 and became foreign minister in 1992. He served concurrently as prime minister from 2007 until Qatar’s 2013 leadership transition, when he left government. During part of that period he also directed the Qatar Investment Authority, but its own mandate identifies it as the State of Qatar’s sovereign wealth fund; those national assets are therefore separate from his personal fortune.

After leaving office, HBJ became more visible as a private investor. Forbes traces his personal wealth to investments and identifies Paramount Services Holdings as his vehicle for a large Deutsche Bank stake acquired after his 2013 departure. Deutsche Bank’s current shareholder disclosure lists Paramount at 4.91 percent. This privately attributed holding, together with other published personal investments, supports Finance & Investments as the best description of his wealth without treating Qatar’s energy income or sovereign portfolio as his own.

After leaving office, HBJ became more visible as a private investor. Forbes traces his personal wealth to investments and identifies Paramount Services Holdings as his vehicle for a large Deutsche Bank stake acquired after his 2013 departure. Deutsche Bank’s current shareholder disclosure lists Paramount at 4.91 percent. This privately attributed holding, together with other published personal investments, supports Finance & Investments as the best description of his wealth without treating Qatar’s energy income or sovereign portfolio as his own.
